NonEleBowRanger1.text:
"Even a lawless land needs rules. Even anarchy requires order." 
- Kylian Cyaxan

NonEleBowRanger2.text: As Cyaxan's criminal empire grew, so too did its need for enforcers. The Trarthan militia was its answer.

NonEleBowRanger3.text: Order came later. At first, the Trarthan militia was little more than muscle - sold to the highest house, and drunk on its coin.

NonEleBowRanger4.text: The Trarthan militia delivers justice swiftly - usually before a crime is even committed.

NonEleBowRanger5.text: "The militia don't keep the peace. They keep Trarthus profitable."

NonEleBowRanger6.text: "They weren't just enforcers. They were reminders - of who ruled Korathin's gutters, and what disobedience cost."

NonEleBowRanger7.text: For a time, the militia had the slums on lockdown. Then Cyaxan flooded them with gems - and the streets ran red with blood.

NonEleBowRanger8.text: Of all Kylian Cyaxan's sins, virtue gems were the most costly. Blinded by greed, he never foresaw the chaos they'd unleash.

NonEleBowRanger9.text: Kylian Cyaxan demanded a swift response to the chaos in the streets. The militia answered - virtue gems in hand.

NonEleBowRanger10.text: The militia met fire with fire - gems for gems, blood for blood.

NonEleBowRanger11.text: With gems came power - and with power came fewer survivors of the militia's 'justice'.

NonEleBowRanger12.text: "They called it peace when the killing slowed. Not justice - just fewer people left to fight back... and even fewer who would dare."

NonEleBowRangerNoble1.text: {0} Cyaxan once kept order in Korathin's worst quarter. Now she keeps trophies instead.

NonEleBowRangerNoble2.text: {0} was born of Cyaxan stock, raised on slum smoke and discipline.

NonEleBowRangerNoble3.text: {0} Cyaxan: a name once feared across the Trarthan militia ranks - feared even more now she's off the leash.

NonEleBowRangerNoble4.text: Trarthus was barren after the Vaal Cataclysm... until the Empire began exiling their unwanted to its bleak shores.

NonEleBowRangerNoble5.text: "Our ancestors were exiled so that the Eternal Empire could have its thousand-year peace. I don't give a damn about Wraeclast."

EleBowRanger1.text: Gems from Trarthus have their own trademarks. Like the populace, they are more brutal.

EleBowRanger2.text: Keitan slaves built the walls of Korathin. Kylian Cyaxan filled them with vice before the mortar had dried.

EleBowRanger3.text: Cyaxan brothels bore no name. But those who entered often forget their own.

EleBowRanger4.text: First came desire. Then came dependency. Cyaxan offered both - by design.

EleBowRanger5.text: The courtesans were Cyaxan's first pushers. Pleasure and powder ensured each customer returned - shaking a little more each time.

EleBowRanger6.text: Most were addicted before they even knew it - such was the potency of Cyaxan's blend.

EleBowRanger7.text: "In the early days, the drug trade was shared. Then Cyaxan made sharing... unprofitable."

EleBowRanger8.text: When even dependency began to dull, Kylian Cyaxan sought something stronger - 'virtue' in crystalline form.

EleBowRanger9.text: While most wielded gems for violence, Kylian Cyaxan saw in them something far more sordid.

EleBowRanger10.text: The first gem-lit flesh in Trarthus didn't belong to a warrior. It belonged to a courtesan.

EleBowRanger12.text: Some gems enhanced sensation. Others suppressed it - turning bodies into tools of compliance.

EleBowRanger13.text: What began as pleasure became ritual. What began as choice became conditioning.

EleBowRanger14.text: "Kylian Cyaxan is long dead - as are many of his customers. But the thing about that kind of customer? They replenish themselves."

EleBowRanger16.text:
"Brick and stone may hold a city... but pleasure holds a people."
 - Kylian Cyaxan

EleBowRangerNoble1.text: {0} Cyaxan knew every back alley in Korathin - especially the ones that glittered.

EleBowRangerNoble2.text: The gems are socketed deep. {0} Cyaxan's need, deeper still.

EleBowRangerNoble3.text: If it glints, {0} Cyaxan follows. If it runs, she chases.

EleBowRangerNoble4.text: "As decaying Empires are wont to do, the use of exile as a punishment gradually became more common over the centuries..."

EleBowRangerNoble5.text: The Eternal Empire eventually made their greatest mistake: they exiled a simple farmer to Trarthus.

MeleeAOEMarauder1.text: In Korathin's slave pits, Keita found its fortune. Death made for eager audiences.

MeleeAOEMarauder2.text: Keitan slaves raised the walls of Korathin. Their blood still clings to the mortar.

MeleeAOEMarauder3.text: House Keita did not always command such fear. It was their crushing of the rebellion that made them a force to be reckoned with.

MeleeAOEMarauder4.text: The slave rebellion began with a whisper. A promise of freedom passed from throat to throat, louder each time.

MeleeAOEMarauder5.text: One night, the chains fell silent. The next, they snapped. Keitans awoke to fire in their camps and blood on their floors.

MeleeAOEMarauder6.text: It took just three days. Three days for Keita to crush the dissidents, reforge the chains, and fill the pits with corpses.

MeleeAOEMarauder7.text: Keita left the rebels hanging, stripped and nameless. Not as martyrs - just meat, gone to waste.

MeleeAOEMarauder8.text: After the revolt, Ixan Keita declared the slaves must be reminded of their place. Thus began the Trarthan slave pits.

MeleeAOEMarauder9.text: From the ashes of rebellion came the slave pit - dug to remind the living what happened to those who sought freedom.

MeleeAOEMarauder10.text: The slave pits are a reflection of Trarthan society: brutal, bloodthirsty, and swift to punish mistakes.

MeleeAOEMarauder11.text: Keita doesn't fear uprisings anymore. Every lash, every cage, every pit - lessons carved in flesh.

MeleeAOEMarauder13.text: "In Trarthus, freedom is earned, not given."

MeleeAOEMarauderNoble1.text: "The lucky ones die early. The rest learn to live with it."

MeleeAOEMarauderNoble2.text: Fighting in chains taught {0} everything he needed - including how to break them.

MeleeAOEMarauderNoble3.text: Inside Trarthus or out, slave or slaver - none bred more enemies than House Keita.

MeleeAOEMarauderNoble4.text: The Trarthans paid back their debt to the Karui, aiding them when it was their turn to battle the Empire.

MeleeAOEMarauderNoble5.text: When Tyndarus Phrecius tried to resupply his occupying legions on Trarthus, the Karui blockaded the Archipelago.

MeleeStrikesMarauder1.text: Trarthan slavers are despicable - and indispensable.

MeleeStrikesMarauder2.text: Of all the Trarthan Death Trades, none strip the soul quite like slavery - brutal in both intent and execution.

MeleeStrikesMarauder15.text: Trarthus was built on the backs of slaves, whose labour shaped much of its infrastructure. At the whip-hand stood House Keita.

MeleeStrikesMarauder4.text: Cruel even by Trarthan standards, House Keita's blend of brutality and efficiency made them ideal architects of the slave trade.

MeleeStrikesMarauder5.text: In their prime, Keita built more than cities - they built leverage. For a time, no House dared challenge their hold on Trarthus.

MeleeStrikesMarauder6.text: Ixan Keita helped build Trarthus - and nearly ruled it. But power begets ambition, and ambition always demands more.

MeleeStrikesMarauder7.text: The ambition of Ixan Keita was his undoing. His bid for power sparked war with Bardiya - a war Keita could not win.

MeleeStrikesMarauder8.text: Keita held the chains. Bardiya cut the purse strings. Trarthus watched as labour lost to leverage - and coin won the war.

MeleeStrikesMarauder9.text: Keita swore fealty to the Council with a clenched jaw. Better a seat at the table than exile from the game entirely.

MeleeStrikesMarauder10.text: Though the Keita of today is still a House of influence, Bardiya remembers their treachery - and limits their power accordingly.

MeleeStrikesMarauder12.text: "House Keita wrote the bloody book on cruelty. Think of the worst bastard you know - either they're a Keitan, or a poor imitation."

MeleeStrikesMarauder13.text: "The Merchant Council's a leash on House Keita - and the irony ain't lost on 'em. Still, better leashed than buried."

MeleeStrikesMarauder14.text:
"Pain is the language of obedience."
 - Ixan Keita

MeleeStrikesMarauderNoble1.text: {0} Keita built his name in the slave pits of Korathin - and built his fortune on the backs beneath him.

MeleeStrikesMarauderNoble2.text: Slaves obeyed. Rivals bled. The rest learned to stay out of {0} Keita's way.

MeleeStrikesMarauderNoble3.text: The pits made killers of men... and monsters of those who ran them.

MeleeStrikesMarauderNoble4.text: For centuries, ash from Karui volcanoes rode the wind to Trarthus. It turned slaves into the continent's finest tools.

MeleeStrikesMarauderNoble5.text: "Slavery began in Trarthus when a simple farmer offered to serve and grow food in exchange for his life. Pathetic... but profitable."

ElementalWitch1.text: Thaumaturgy in Trarthus is like smoke in the lungs - unpleasant, expected, and always present.

ElementalWitch2.text: Before vice, before gems, before brothels and powder - Cyaxan dealt in spices, cloth and coin.

ElementalWitch3.text: "They all started legitimate - even Cyaxan. But virtue doesn't buy power. Vice does."

ElementalWitch4.text: Cyaxan didn't need blades. They had margins - and the power that comes from knowing what everyone else wanted.

ElementalWitch5.text: In time, margins thinned. Rivals grew bolder. So Cyaxan found new markets - darker ones.

ElementalWitch6.text: Cyaxan didn't set out to rule the underworld. Only to survive it. Then survival turned to opportunity.

ElementalWitch7.text: Kylian Cyaxan's ascent to lord of the Trarthan underworld was not without obstacles. The first arose within his own house.

ElementalWitch8.text: Kylian's first victim wasn't a member of a rival House - it was family. From then on, betrayal became tradition.

ElementalWitch9.text: Kylian Cyaxan never raised his voice. Just his glass. The rest of the table never stood again.

ElementalWitch10.text: With rivals dead or disgraced, Kylian moved fast - consolidating power, ensuring no Cyaxan could rise as he had.

ElementalWitch11.text: Kylian never trusted alliances. He preferred leverage. Internally, that meant secrets. Externally, sabotage.

ElementalWitch13.text: "When dining with a Cyaxan, bring an appetite - and an antidote."

ElementalWitch14.text: Cyaxan rarely availed themselves of House Azadi's services. They preferred less... bloody methods.

ElementalWitchNoble1.text: It wasn't people {0} Cyaxan loathed, but the frailties they wore so proudly: need, artifice, expectation.

ElementalWitchNoble2.text: Cold, restrained, detached - anathema to Cyaxan ideals. But death has many forms, and {0} excelled in hers.

ElementalWitchNoble3.text: {0} Cyaxan despised mess - of thought, of feeling, of flesh.

ElementalWitchNoble4.text: "Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius was a fool who let a wasteland full of exiles defy the Empire."

ElementalWitchNoble5.text: "Trarthus lives on, long after the dying husk of its parent Empire has become nothing but a memory."

ChaosMinionWitch1.text: In the early days of Trarthus, each House kept to its corner. Peace held - not through trust, but through distance.

ChaosMinionWitch2.text: As each House drifted from legitimacy to vice, conflict was inevitable. Kylian Cyaxan made sure of it.

ChaosMinionWitch3.text: "They say Kylian Cyaxan was once an upstanding merchant. But then, they say a lot of things."

ChaosMinionWitch4.text:
"To play both sides well is to leave no fingerprints - only consequences."
 - Kylian Cyaxan

ChaosMinionWitch5.text: History blames Bardiya and Keita for the Merchant Wars. Fewer recall that Cyaxan was whispering in both ears all along.

ChaosMinionWitch6.text: As Bardiya and Keita went to war, Kylian Cyaxan stayed neutral - by selling secrets to both sides.

ChaosMinionWitch7.text: "A Cyaxan will stir the pot, watch it boil, then let others burn their hands - all while they slip out the back door."

ChaosMinionWitch8.text:
"There's coin in war... so long as you're not the one fighting it."
 - Kylian Cyaxan

ChaosMinionWitch9.text: The Merchant Wars began with tariffs and treaties. They ended with fire, famine, and grudges that would last a lifetime.

ChaosMinionWitch10.text: When all was said and done, the Merchant Wars had made fortunes for the few - and graves for the many.

ChaosMinionWitch11.text: Cyaxan may have lit the fire. But when bodies piled high and profits ran dry, even Kylian sought peace.

ChaosMinionWitch12.text: The end of the Merchant Wars came not from diplomacy, but depletion. The Houses didn't shake hands - they paused to reload.

ChaosMinionWitch13.text: No House admits to starting the Merchant Wars. But every House claims to have won them.

ChaosMinionWitchNoble1.text: Some Cyaxans peddled pleasure, others poison. {0} Cyaxan peddled death.

ChaosMinionWitchNoble2.text: Even {0}'s fellow Cyaxans questioned her methods. But never their efficacy.

ChaosMinionWitchNoble3.text: Few in Trarthus kill with curses or corpses. But those who do face no fear of retribution.

ChaosMinionWitchNoble4.text: "They exiled their undesirables to Trarthus, and then had the gall to act surprised when those undesirables refused to bow down."

ChaosMinionWitchNoble5.text: "Witches aren't feared in Trarthus. They're adored. We wisely sided with the rebels against Little Tinny Phrecius."

PhysConvertTemplar1.text: In Trarthus, faith never died. It just turned inward.

PhysConvertTemplar2.text: The major Houses didn't worship gods. They tried to become them.

PhysConvertTemplar3.text: Divinity demands belief. Trarthus demanded proof.

PhysConvertTemplar4.text: One claimed the mantle of flame. Another of blood. But in a city of rival 'gods', none rose above the noise.

PhysConvertTemplar5.text: A House could rise through war, through gold, through secrets - but not through grace.

PhysConvertTemplar6.text: Ixan Keita declared himself a god - and built temples to prove it. His slaves were given no choice but to pray.

PhysConvertTemplar7.text: In his quest for Divinity, Ixan Keita demanded worship. Obedience was beaten in. But no man ever reached godhood through fear alone.

PhysConvertTemplar8.text: They sang of Ixan Keita, knelt in his hollow shrines... but their hearts spoke only of hate.

PhysConvertTemplar9.text: Ixan mistook silence for reverence. In truth, not one soul believed. And so he remained just that: a mortal soul.

PhysConvertTemplar10.text:
"Let them hate me, if they must. Even hatred bows to power."
 - Ixan Keita

PhysConvertTemplar11.text: They preached in alleyways and taverns. Few listened. Fewer remembered.

PhysConvertTemplar12.text: Attempts to bring organised religion to Trarthus were many - and all of them met with blood.

PhysConvertTemplar13.text: Faith is tolerated in Trarthus - but only so long as it is kept to one's self.

PhysConvertTemplar14.text: Even the pious stray in Trarthus - led not by devils, but by gold and supple skin.

PhysConvertTemplar15.text: Trarthans revere but one god: the almighty coin.

PhysConvertTemplar16.text:
"If your mission should take you to Trarthus, you'd best carry a knife."
 - Gospel and Blade

PhysConvertTemplarNoble1.text: {0} Keita came to preach salvation. He left certain there was none to be found.

PhysConvertTemplarNoble2.text: In a city built on secrets, faith never stood a chance.

PhysConvertTemplarNoble3.text: Though born of Keita blood, {0} sought to better Trarthus through faith - until his kin reminded him where power truly lay.

PhysConvertTemplarNoble4.text: Once Emperor Tyndarus caught wind of Trarthan warlords setting up a society, he sent his legions to stomp them back down.

PhysConvertTemplarNoble5.text: The Phrecian legions executed the warlords of that era, and instituted crushing taxes on the budding Trarthan society.

AurasMinionsTemplar1.text: Some foreigners cling to warm memories of Divinity. In Trarthus, that's considered true madness.

AurasMinionsTemplar2.text: Trarthans know Innocence not as a god, but as a tale told by passing missionaries - and quickly forgotten.

AurasMinionsTemplar3.text: "A fire that does not warm, does not feed, does not kill... what use is it in Trarthus?"

AurasMinionsTemplar4.text: Innocence preaches purity. Trarthus breeds survival. The two have little in common.

AurasMinionsTemplar5.text: "When they call Korathin a city of sin, they're not talking about the god."

AurasMinionsTemplar6.text: "Some say there's no honour left in Korathin. Others say it never belonged here to begin with."

AurasMinionsTemplar7.text: A good deed in Trarthus gets you one thing: a target on your back.

AurasMinionsTemplar8.text: "What's a man to do with morals, when no one else plays by them?"

AurasMinionsTemplar10.text: Even in Trarthus, someone buries the bodies. Someone remembers the names.

AurasMinionsTemplar11.text: Some virtues endure - not in law, nor gods, but in spite of both.

AurasMinionsTemplar12.text: The surest way to frighten Ixan Keita was kindness. Always hunting for an angle, he could never see it for what it was.

AurasMinionsTemplar13.text: Keita drew brutes from every corner - sadists, zealots, and worse. What bound them was a taste for cruelty.

AurasMinionsTemplarNoble1.text: They mocked {0} Keita's prayers. Until one day, the sinner burned, and they said nothing more.

AurasMinionsTemplarNoble2.text: Trarthus could not unmake {0} Keita's faith. But it tried. With ridicule. With pain. With temptation.

AurasMinionsTemplarNoble3.text: Innocence found no altar in Trarthus. Just one man.

AurasMinionsTemplarNoble4.text: In 870 IC, the four great Founders spurred their guerrilla rebellion into open warfare against the occupying legions.

AurasMinionsTemplarNoble5.text: It took two years of open warfare, but Tyndarus finally capitulated in exchange for the lives of his legions.

PhysicalDuelist1.text: Trarthus was lawless once - but not without rules. Some approached the Death Trades with grace... and surprising decorum.

PhysicalDuelist2.text: Before the Merchant Wars. Before the Council. Before Trarthus had a name. There was the Code.

PhysicalDuelist4.text: The Trarthan Code was not written - not at first. It was remembered. Passed in whispers, etched in scars.

PhysicalDuelist5.text: "Break the Code, and you risked more than your life. You risked your name."

PhysicalDuelist6.text: Whether in gutters or along trade routes, the Code took root where laws could not.

PhysicalDuelist7.text: House Bardiya were first to back the Code - an early sign of their predilection for order and control.

PhysicalDuelist8.text: To House Azadi, the Code wasn't a set of rules. It was a contract. And they never broke contracts.

PhysicalDuelist9.text: Cyaxan did not endorse the Code. Not at first. They waited, watched, and once it took hold, claimed they'd backed it all along.

PhysicalDuelist10.text: Even House Keita, for all their brutality, bowed to the Code. Not out of respect - but survival.

PhysicalDuelist11.text: Even under Council rule, the Code endures - now etched into law.

PhysicalDuelist12.text: "Travel to Trarthus is discouraged. Should you go, learn the Code - and honour it." - A Merchant's Guide to Trarthus

PhysicalDuelist13.text: "Break the Trarthan Code and you'll likely be buried by someone who didn't." - A Merchant's Guide to Trarthus

PhysicalDuelist14.text:
"Those under the Great Houses shall answer any blood wager issued." 
- Trarthan Code, Article V

PhysicalDuelistNoble1.text: {0} Azadi's words? Withering. His blade? Equally so.

PhysicalDuelistNoble2.text:
"Elegance is not lost in violence - only in vulgarity."
 - {0} Azadi

PhysicalDuelistNoble3.text:
"Ask any Azadin... You don't get rich in Trarthus by being bad in a fight."
 - {0} Azadi

PhysicalDuelistNoble4.text: "The four Great Founders were not exiles. 'Twas the first Trarthan-born generation, once we actually had a modicum of society going."

PhysicalDuelistNoble5.text: The four Great Houses were once begrudging allies, fighting a guerilla war against occupying legions.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist1.text: Violence has always been common in Trarthus. But it was Ratha Azadi who commodified it - turned it into an art form all her own.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist2.text: Azadi distinguished itself not through efficiency, but through audacious spectacle. Azadins didn't kill. They wove death itself.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist3.text: Ratha Azadi understood that killing goes beyond the act itself. Some kills live longer than the killer - but only when done right.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist4.text: "Anywhere else, you'd kill from the shadows. But this is Trarthus - so we shout murder from the rooftops." - Ratha Azadi

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist5.text: Would-be sadists flocked to House Azadi, seeking kin in their band of killers. But only a select few rose above the chaff.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist7.text: Among Azadi's best, the mark mattered less than the method. To kill without flair was crude - commonplace.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist8.text: A name etched in blood is still a name. Many Azadins died trying to earn theirs.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist9.text: Azadi's finest were known for rivalry as much as skill. On one occasion, both died trying to outdo the other - while their mark fled.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist10.text: Audacious though they may be, Azadins don't advertise. They let their work speak for itself.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist11.text: Failure rang loudest of all. A botched kill meant the replacement made an example - of both target and Azadin.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist12.text:
"Anyone can kill. We give death a name, a face, a reputation."
 - Ratha Azadi

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelist13.text: "Those bloody Azadins...  Could kill twice the people in half the time if they weren't so obsessed with 'artistry'." - Ixan Keita

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelistNoble1.text:
"Who needs paint, when blood spills so beautifully?"
 - {0} Azadi

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelistNoble2.text: {0} Azadi's blade did more than silence. It left an impression.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelistNoble3.text: {0} Azadi: proof that his House's legacy wasn't written in history - but carved into flesh.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelistNoble4.text: Tyndarus tried to sail reinforcements west, but the Ezomytes burned his ships in the night, and supplied poisoned grain at port.

MeleeAOEStrikeDuelistNoble5.text: "Trarthus didn't even ask the Ezomytes to aid them in the uprising. Those beautiful poetic bastards did it all on their own."

DiverMercenary1.text: House Azadi's reach extends even to the sea floor. There is nowhere they cannot find you.

DiverMercenary2.text: Ratha would sooner string you up than send you to a watery grave. But sometimes, killers can't be choosers.

DiverMercenary3.text: Ratha's wrath knew no bounds. Some ran from it. Others revelled in it.

TrapsMinesShadow1.text: The children of Korathin don't play in fields. They play in slag.

TrapsMinesShadow2.text: The fields were quiet. The factories never were. One bred men. The other broke them.

TrapsMinesShadow3.text: A Trarthan farmer's back bends with harvest. A cityman's with hunger.

TrapsMinesShadow4.text: To the cityfolk, a broken tool is replaced. To the peasant, it's a week lost.

TrapsMinesShadow5.text: The fields breed silence. The cities breed noise. Neither understands the other's music.

TrapsMinesShadow6.text: "Out in the country, a harvest is shared. Here in the city, it's sold - then stolen back."

TrapsMinesShadow9.text: Korathin's smog doesn't just fill the sky. It seeps behind the eyes.

TrapsMinesShadow10.text: A thousand chimneys mark the skyline - monuments to what Trarthus built, and what it buried.

TrapsMinesShadow12.text: No songs are sung in Korathin factories. Just the rhythm of toil and breaking backs.

TrapsMinesShadowNoble1.text: Though rotten to the bone, Trarthus still shelters those the world cast aside.

TrapsMinesShadowNoble2.text: A Mirror of Delirium cracked {0} Azadi's mind like glass - or so the story goes.

TrapsMinesShadowNoble3.text: To House Azadi, {0} is a relic. To everyone else, a warning.

TrapsMinesShadowNoble4.text: "The moment the four Great Founders actually won their war of independence, tensions began to rise between them."

TrapsMinesShadowNoble5.text: "The four great Founders were only allies out of necessity. It didn't take much for their hard-won independence to fall apart."

Crit1HShadow1.text: Azadi was last to rise among the major Houses. Where killing was common, no one paid for it  - until Azadi cornered the market.

Crit1HShadow2.text: At first, anyone could kill for coin. House Azadi made the kill itself worth paying for.

Crit1HShadow3.text: Independent killers didn't last. Clients knew: hire Azadi, or become their next contract.

Crit1HShadow4.text: "When palms need greasing, you go to House Bardiya. When heads need rolling, you send for House Azadi."

Crit1HShadow5.text: "A masterful blend of audacity and discretion - that's the Azadi trademark. You'll know who made the kill, never who paid for it."

Crit1HShadow6.text: Azadi's true currency wasn't coin. It was reputation. And reputation, once wounded, bled.

Crit1HShadow7.text: Azadi contracts came sealed in wax. To break the seal was to accept the mark - and the consequences of failure.

Crit1HShadow8.text: Each Azadi contract was coded - names obscured, motives buried. But the message was always the same: kill.

Crit1HShadow9.text: Some left trophies. Others left warnings. But all Azadins left a message: the job was done - and the debt had been paid.

Crit1HShadow10.text: "Everyone knows: renege on Azadi, and become their next target."

Crit1HShadow11.text: "To last in House Azadi, you need to be dead inside - or skilled at making others so. Preferably both."

Crit1HShadow13.text:
"In Trarthus, life is cheap. We made sure death wasn't."
 - Ratha Azadi

Crit1HShadowNoble1.text: {0} Azadi's was not a style. It was a standard - silent, surgical, untraceable.

Crit1HShadowNoble2.text: Where other Azadi painted death in crimson arcs, {0} delivered it with a whisper.

Crit1HShadowNoble3.text: In a House that prized spectacle, {0} Azadi offered none - only results.

Crit1HShadowNoble4.text: "Trarthans never forget a debt. When the Ezomytes rebelled against the Empire, even though centuries had passed, we came to their aid."

Crit1HShadowNoble5.text: "Once our debts were paid to the Ezomytes and the Karui, we considered ourselves even. After that... well, might makes right."

MiscScion1.text: The Merchant Council gave Trarthus a mask of order. Those who can't wear it are cast out.

MiscScion2.text: Though they would not rule for years, the Bardiyans helped shape Trarthus - quiet power moving behind every deal and coin exchange.

MiscScion3.text: The first Bardiyan vault was carved into Korathin's bedrock - long before the city rose above it.

MiscScion4.text: While the Keitans laid stone, the Bardiyans moved coin. One built a city in broad daylight. The other ran it from the shadows.

MiscScion5.text: Before the wars, there was trade. Keitan muscle, Bardiyan mind. Neither trusted the other - but both saw profit.

MiscScion6.text: No two Trarthan forefathers were more opposed - in ideology or in temperament - than Ixan Keita and Quilon Bardiya.

MiscScion7.text: Keita and Bardiya's rivalry erupted across Trarthus - supply lines cut, coin vanished, and not a single soldier raised.

MiscScion8.text: Keita demanded tribute. Bardiya and Azadi refused. The result: starvation, sabotage, and blood in the streets of Korathin.

MiscScion9.text: Bardiya won their struggle with Keita. Coin proved more vital to Trarthus than all the slaves Keita could whip into labour.

MiscScion10.text: Bardiya's victory over Keita came at a cost. From that pyrrhic win grew the Merchant Council - cooperative in name, Bardiyan in truth.

MiscScion11.text: House Bardiya remains as its forefather left it: clever, conniving, and always listening.

MiscScion12.text:
"A whisper in the right ear is stronger than any army."
 - Quilon Bardiya

MiscScion13.text: "To rule through fear is to court your own demise. A frightened animal lashes out. A content one purrs in your lap." - Quilon Bardiya

MiscScion14.text: "Bardiyans are clever, aye - but so ruthlessly self-serving it's a wonder their banquets don't end in blood."

MiscScionNoble1.text: {0} was born into Bardiyan silk and silver - until a sibling whispered her inheritance away...

MiscScionNoble2.text: {0} Bardiya's legacy was stolen. Her appetite remains.

MiscScionNoble3.text: Betrayal is currency in House Bardiya. {0} has never left a ledger unsettled.

MiscScionNoble4.text: The Eternal Empire stopped exiling people to Trarthus after 872 IC. They began building island prisons closer to home instead.

MiscScionNoble5.text: "The Empire essentially cut contact with Trarthus for five hundred years... until Chitus wanted our powder."

AurasMinionsTemplarNobleNeon1.text:
'A ruckus that is made, may not be unmade.'
 - Trarthan Code Appendice XII
